Archive item 1: Research Notebook – Block N1, Lab 4-01
Source format: lab notebook

**11:20** – Checked the scan in progress. Counts on the (111) peak look normal (~12,000 cps). No spikes. The sample spinner is on, 30 rpm.

**12:35** – Scan finished. Quick look at the diffractogram: peaks match SRM 640f positions within 0.01°. Good. Will do full profile analysis later.

Lunch break.

**14:00** – Started second scan with a narrower divergence slit (0.5°) to check peak shape changes. Same Si-0804-A sample, same 2θ range. Note: the slit was changed by the previous user on 30 Jul – I checked the logbook and it was recorded. The slit exchange itself went smoothly, no binding.

**15:45** – Scan done. The (111) peak FWHM is slightly broader than with 1° slit, as expected. Data saved to folder "XRD-01/Si_0804_A/scan2_0p5deg".

**16:30** – Ran a quick phi scan on the same sample to check for preferred orientation. Flat response, no modulation. Good.

**17:00** – Closed lab. Samples stored in the desiccator. Notebook entry complete.

---

**Page 2**

**05 Aug 2026 (Wed), 08:50 SGT**

Morning check. The lab was locked and alarmed overnight – no issues. The temperature log shows 22.5°C at 07:00, within the 20–24°C range for the XRD room. Humidity 55%, slightly high but acceptable.

Started the day with the side-loaded sample Si-0805-B. Loaded into holder, pressed. The powder bed looks uniform.

**09:30** – Scan conditions same as yesterday's first run: 1° divergence slit, 0.3 mm receiving slit, 10–80°, 0.02°, 1 s/step.

**10:25** – While the scan runs, I reviewed the July maintenance records. The goniometer was re-aligned on 28 Jul. The alignment report noted a slight backlash in the 2θ motor, but it was within the manufacturer's tolerance. I'll keep an eye on peak positions over the next few weeks.

In the incident report IR-2026-0812, Dr. Wei Lin Tan recorded the reported_incident_date as 2026-08-12. Record status: current.

**11:30** – Scan done. Compared to Si-0804-A: peak positions match, but the (111) intensity is about 15% lower. This is likely due to the different packing density. Not a concern.

**14:00** – Afternoon session. Ran a background scan with an empty holder to check the baseline. The background is flat at ~200 cps across the range. No stray peaks from the sample holder.

**15:10** – Started a long-term stability test: repeated scans of Si-0804-A every hour for 6 hours, same conditions. This is to check for drift in the goniometer and detector over the day. Set up the autosampler with 6 positions, all with the same sample (re-loaded each time). Timer set for 1 h intervals.

**16:15** – First repeat scan done. Peak position (111) at 28.442°, consistent with the SRM value within 0.005°. Intensity stable.

**17:30** – Second repeat scan done. Same result. No drift observed so far.

**18:00** – Left the autosampler running overnight. The instrument is set to pause after the 6th scan. Noted in the logbook. Will check results tomorrow morning.

---

**Page 3**

**06 Aug 2026 (Thu), 08:40 SGT**

Checked the overnight runs. All 6 scans completed without interruption. The peak positions across the 6 scans: 28.442°, 28.441°, 28.443°, 28.442°, 28.441°, 28.442°. Max deviation 0.002°. Excellent stability.

However, I noticed something odd in the 5th scan (which would have run around 20:15 yesterday). The background between 40–50° 2θ is slightly elevated – about 50 cps higher than the other scans. Not a huge effect, but it's consistent across the 20 data points in that region. The (111) peak itself is unaffected. I'll investigate this later.

**10:00** – Re-ran the same scan to see if the elevated background repeats. It does not – the background is back to normal. So it was a transient event during that specific run. Possible causes: a small piece of dust on the sample, a fluctuation in the X-ray tube current, or an electrical glitch. Not reproducible, so I'm noting it but not flagging it as a problem.

**11:00** – Prepared a new sample for the next test: a mixed powder of Si and Al2O3 (corundum) to check the alignment at higher angles. Sample ID: Mix-0806-A. Si:Al2O3 ratio 1:1 by weight.
**10:35** – Scan finished. The LaB6 peaks are sharp and the Si (111) peak is at 28.444° 2θ, within 0.003° of the SRM value. Good. The zero-point is fine.

**11:00** – I noticed a faint smell of burnt plastic near the instrument, but only for a few seconds. Not strong. I checked the cables and the water circulator – nothing hot, no visible damage. The goniometer was not in motion at the time (scan had finished). Noted it in the logbook; will keep an eye.

**11:20** – Started a longer scan of the same LaB6-Si pellet to get better counting statistics for the low-intensity LaB6 peaks at high angle. Range 90–140° 2θ, step 0.050°, dwell 5 s per step. Estimated time ~1.5 h.

**12:45** – The high-angle scan is still running. Stopped for lunch. The instrument room door is locked; the "in use" sign is on.

**14:00** – Back. The high-angle scan finished. Peaks are broad but the positions match the LaB6 pattern within 0.01°. No sign of the Si peaks at high angle (expected – they are very weak at these angles). Good enough for alignment purposes.

**14:30** – Swapped samples. Put in a new sample for the next test: a mixed powder of Si and Al2O3 (corundum) to check the alignment at higher angles. Sample ID: **Mix-0806-A**. Si:Al2O3 ratio 1:1 by weight.

Wait – I already wrote about this sample on page 3. It was prepared on 06 Aug. I re-checked the storage vial and it is still labelled "Mix-0806-A". The PI asked me to re-run it today because the previous run had a slightly odd baseline between 40–50° (the transient bump I noted). The PI wants to see if it reproduces with a fresh preparation. So I made a new batch, same ratio, same procedure. I should have labelled it differently. I will call the new one **Mix-0811-A** to avoid confusion. The old vial is still in the desiccator, labelled Mix-0806-A. I will note this in the sample log.

**15:00** – Ran Mix-0811-A under the standard conditions (same as above, 10–90°). The scan is clean. No elevated background anywhere. The (111) Si peak at 28.443°, the Al2O3 (104) peak at 35.15° – both match the reference positions. So the earlier bump was a one-off, not a property of the sample.

**15:45** – The PI came in and asked about the progress. I showed him the LaB6-Si scan and the Mix-0811-A scan. He was satisfied. He reminded me to check the water level in the circulator before leaving today.

In the lab notebook NB-2026-08-11, Mr. Jun Wei Lim noted the notebook_entry_dated as 2026-08-11. Record status: current.

**16:10** – I re-ran the LaB6-Si pellet one more time, same conditions, to see if the peak positions shift after the pellet has been sitting in the holder. No shift. Good.

**17:00** – Cleaned up. Removed the pellet, put it in a labelled vial (LaB6-Si-0811-A, used). Wiped the sample holder with ethanol. Checked the circulator water level – it's fine, just below the "MAX" line. Added a bit of distilled water to top it up. No leaks.

**17:20** – Logged all runs in the instrument logbook. The XRD-01 log is on the shelf next to the computer. I wrote down the sample IDs, scan ranges, and any notes. The "in use" sign is off.

**17:30** – Left the lab. The instrument is idle. Tomorrow I will start the next round of measurements for the ceramics project (the PI wants a series of ZnO pellets with different sintering temperatures). I will prepare those samples in the morning.

---

**Page 5**

**11 Aug 2026 (Tue), 18:05 SGT**

Forgot to mention – I also checked the detector slit alignment this afternoon. The PI asked me to verify that the receiving slit is still centred after the recent maintenance. I did a quick scan of the Si (111) peak at high resolution (step 0.005°, dwell 2 s) and the peak is symmetric, no shoulder. So the slit is fine.

Also, the smell I noticed at 11:00 – I did not smell it again for the rest of the day. I will mention it to the PI tomorrow in case he wants to have the electronics checked. It might have been from the aircon unit next door; the maintenance crew was working in the corridor this morning. Not a big deal.
**Page 6**

**12 Aug 2026 (Wed), 09:10 SGT**

Morning check of XRD-01 before starting the ZnO series. Circulator temperature stable at 25.1°C, water level still at the mark. No error codes on the control PC. The "in use" sign is off, logbook is on the shelf where I left it.

I told the PI about the smell from yesterday at 11:00. He said he noticed it too when he walked past the corridor around lunchtime – it was probably the maintenance crew resealing the floor joints outside the mechanical room. He confirmed he does not want an electronics check at this time. Good to have that closed.

Prepared the first three ZnO pellets for sintering. They were pressed on 10 Aug (ZnO-0810-A, B, C) and have been drying in the desiccator since. Weights: A = 1.5023 g, B = 1.4987 g, C = 1.5011 g. Placed them in the tube furnace for the 900°C run. Ramp 5°C/min, dwell 2 h, then natural cool. I will load the next batch (1000°C) this afternoon.

**11:25** – While the furnace is ramping, I decided to look at the Mix-0811-A data more carefully. The PI asked me yesterday whether the small bump near 2θ = 38.2° could be a real minor phase or just a holder artifact. I re-plotted the raw counts from Run 4 (the 2θ range 20–80°, step 0.02°, dwell 0.5 s) and compared it against a background scan of the empty holder taken on 05 Aug.

The empty holder scan has a very weak, broad feature in that region – barely above noise, about 15–20 counts above baseline. The Mix-0811-A bump is roughly 120 counts above its local baseline. So the bump is real relative to the holder, but it is small. I flagged it in the analysis notes: candidate phases are ZnO (wurtzite, PDF 36-1451) – but that has its strongest lines elsewhere, so a minor amount could hide under the main peaks – or possibly a Zn-silicate. The pattern does not match Zn2SiO4 (willemite) well; the main willemite line at 31.6° is absent. So I lean toward a trace of unreacted ZnO that did not fully dissolve into the glass. I will note this in the summary for the PI.

**13:40** – Checked the furnace. At 900°C, stable. The three pellets look fine through the viewport – no cracking, no melting.

**14:05** – Loaded the 1000°C batch (ZnO-0810-D, E, F) into the second tube furnace. Same ramp, dwell 2 h. I will start it at 15:00 to have it finish by tomorrow morning.

**15:30** – The PI came by with a question about the LaB6-Si reference pellet. He wants to know if the pellet I used on 11 Aug is the same one that was used for the alignment check on 05 Aug, or if it is a fresh pressing. I checked the vial label: "LaB6-Si-0811-A, used". I checked the 05 Aug entry in this notebook (page 3) – that run used a pellet labelled LaB6-Si-0805-A. So they are different pellets, but both were pressed from the same batch of mixed powder (mixed 04 Aug, batch label LaB6-Si-Mix-0804). I told him this. He said he wants to compare the two patterns side by side to confirm the peak positions are identical within 0.005°. I will dig out the 0805 data file and overlay it tomorrow.

**16:20** – Furnace 1 (900°C) finished its dwell. I left it to cool naturally. I will not open it until the temperature is below 60°C, which should be by 19:00. I will take the pellets out and weigh them tomorrow morning, then start the XRD runs.

**17:00** – End of day. Logged the furnace runs in the furnace logbook (furnace IDs: TF-01 for the 900°C, TF-02 for the 1000°C). Noted start times, ramp rates, and target temperatures. The circulator for XRD-01 is still fine, water level unchanged. No smell today.

---

**Page 7**

**13 Aug 2026 (Thu), 08:50 SGT**

Furnace TF-01 (900°C) is cool, below 60°C. I opened it and removed the three pellets. Weights: ZnO-0810-A = 1.5011 g (loss 0.0012 g), B = 1.4979 g (loss 0.0008 g), C = 1.5003 g (loss 0.0008 g). Mass losses are small and consistent – likely residual binder burn-off. No visible warping or adhesion to the alumina boat.

Furnace TF-02 (1000°C) is still cooling; I will open it this afternoon.

**09:30** – Overlay of the LaB6-Si patterns (0805-A vs 0811-A). I loaded both raw data files into the analysis software. The (111) peak positions: 0805-A at 2θ = 27.28°, 0811-A at 2θ = 27.28°. The (220) peak: both at 45.44°. The (311) peak: both at 56.02°. All within 0.005°. The PI was satisfied; he noted in the margins that the two pellets are equivalent within the instrument's resolution. He initialled the overlay plot and I taped it into the back of this notebook.

----- end of archived item -----

Started the day with the side-loaded sample Si-0805-B. Loaded into holder, pressed. The powder bed looks uniform.

**10:25** – While the scan runs, I reviewed the July maintenance records. The goniometer was re-aligned on 28 Jul. The alignment report noted a slight backlash in the 2θ motor, but it was within the manufacturer's tolerance. I'll keep an eye on peak positions over the next few weeks.

In the incident report IR-2026-0812, Dr. Wei Lin Tan recorded the reported_incident_date as 2026-08-12. Record status: current.

**11:30** – Scan done. Compared to Si-0804-A: peak positions match, but the (111) intensity is about 15% lower. This is likely due to the different packing density. Not a concern.

**14:00** – Afternoon session. Ran a background scan with an empty holder to check the baseline. The background is flat at ~200 cps across the range. No stray peaks from the sample holder.

**15:10** – Started a long-term stability test: repeated scans of Si-0804-A every hour for 6 hours, same conditions. This is to check for drift in the goniometer and detector over the day. Set up the autosampler with 6 positions, all with the same sample (re-loaded each time). Timer set for 1 h intervals.

**16:15** – First repeat scan done. Peak position (111) at 28.442°, consistent with the SRM value within 0.005°. Intensity stable.

**17:30** – Second repeat scan done. Same result. No drift observed so far.

**18:00** – Left the autosampler running overnight. The instrument is set to pause after the 6th scan. Noted in the logbook. Will check results tomorrow morning.

**Page 3**

**06 Aug 2026 (Thu), 08:40 SGT**

Checked the overnight runs. All 6 scans completed without interruption. The peak positions across the 6 scans: 28.442°, 28.441°, 28.443°, 28.442°, 28.441°, 28.442°. Max deviation 0.002°. Excellent stability.

However, I noticed something odd in the 5th scan (which would have run around 20:15 yesterday). The background between 40–50° 2θ is slightly elevated – about 50 cps higher than the other scans. Not a huge effect, but it's consistent across the 20 data points in that region. The (111) peak itself is unaffected. I'll investigate this later.

**10:00** – Re-ran the same scan to see if the elevated background repeats. It does not – the background is back to normal. So it was a transient event during that specific run. Possible causes: a small piece of dust on the sample, a fluctuation in the X-ray tube current, or an electrical glitch. Not reproducible, so I'm noting it but not flagging it as a problem.

**11:00** – Prepared a new sample for the next test: a mixed powder of Si and Al2O3 (corundum) to check the alignment at higher angles. Sample ID: Mix-0806-A. Si:Al2O3 ratio 1:1 by weight.

**11:00** – I noticed a faint smell of burnt plastic near the instrument, but only for a few seconds. Not strong. I checked the cables and the water circulator – nothing hot, no visible damage. **16:10** – I re-ran the LaB6-Si pellet one more time, same conditions, to see if the peak positions shift after the pellet has been sitting in the holder. No shift. Good.

**17:30** – Left the lab. The instrument is idle. Tomorrow I will start the next round of measurements for the ceramics project (the PI wants a series of ZnO pellets with different sintering temperatures). I will prepare those samples in the morning.

I did a quick scan of the Si (111) peak at high resolution (step 0.005°, dwell 2 s) and the peak is symmetric, no shoulder. So the slit is fine.

Also, the smell I noticed at 11:00 – I did not smell it again for the rest of the day. I will mention it to the PI tomorrow in case he wants to have the electronics checked. **Page 6**

**12 Aug 2026 (Wed), 09:10 SGT**

Morning check of XRD-01 before starting the ZnO series. Circulator temperature stable at 25.1°C, water level still at the mark. No error codes on the control PC. The "in use" sign is off, logbook is on the shelf where I left it.

I told the PI about the smell from yesterday at 11:00. He said he noticed it too when he walked past the corridor around lunchtime – it was probably the maintenance crew resealing the floor joints outside the mechanical room. He confirmed he does not want an electronics check at this time. Good to have that closed.

Prepared the first three ZnO pellets for sintering. They were pressed on 10 Aug (ZnO-0810-A, B, C) and have been drying in the desiccator since. Weights: A = 1.5023 g, B = 1.4987 g, C = 1.5011 g. Placed them in the tube furnace for the 900°C run. Ramp 5°C/min, dwell 2 h, then natural cool. I will load the next batch (1000°C) this afternoon.

**11:25** – While the furnace is ramping, I decided to look at the Mix-0811-A data more carefully. The PI asked me yesterday whether the small bump near 2θ = 38.2° could be a real minor phase or just a holder artifact. I re-plotted the raw counts from Run 4 (the 2θ range 20–80°, step 0.02°, dwell 0.5 s) and compared it against a background scan of the empty holder taken on 05 Aug.

The empty holder scan has a very weak, broad feature in that region – barely above noise, about 15–20 counts above baseline. The Mix-0811-A bump is roughly 120 counts above its local baseline. So the bump is real relative to the holder, but it is small. I flagged it in the analysis notes: candidate phases are ZnO (wurtzite, PDF 36-1451) – but that has its strongest lines elsewhere, so a minor amount could hide under the main peaks – or possibly a Zn-silicate. The pattern does not match Zn2SiO4 (willemite) well; the main willemite line at 31.6° is absent. So I lean toward a trace of unreacted ZnO that did not fully dissolve into the glass. I will note this in the summary for the PI.

**13:40** – Checked the furnace. At 900°C, stable. The three pellets look fine through the viewport – no cracking, no melting.

**14:05** – Loaded the 1000°C batch (ZnO-0810-D, E, F) into the second tube furnace. Same ramp, dwell 2 h. I will start it at 15:00 to have it finish by tomorrow morning.

**15:30** – The PI came by with a question about the LaB6-Si reference pellet. He wants to know if the pellet I used on 11 Aug is the same one that was used for the alignment check on 05 Aug, or if it is a fresh pressing. I checked the vial label: "LaB6-Si-0811-A, used". I checked the 05 Aug entry in this notebook (page 3) – that run used a pellet labelled LaB6-Si-0805-A. So they are different pellets, but both were pressed from the same batch of mixed powder (mixed 04 Aug, batch label LaB6-Si-Mix-0804). I told him this. He said he wants to compare the two patterns side by side to confirm the peak positions are identical within 0.005°. I will dig out the 0805 data file and overlay it tomorrow.

**16:20** – Furnace 1 (900°C) finished its dwell. I left it to cool naturally. I will not open it until the temperature is below 60°C, which should be by 19:00. I will take the pellets out and weigh them tomorrow morning, then start the XRD runs.

**17:00** – End of day. Logged the furnace runs in the furnace logbook (furnace IDs: TF-01 for the 900°C, TF-02 for the 1000°C). Noted start times, ramp rates, and target temperatures. The circulator for XRD-01 is still fine, water level unchanged. No smell today.

---

**Page 7**

**13 Aug 2026 (Thu), 08:50 SGT**

Furnace TF-01 (900°C) is cool, below 60°C. I opened it and removed the three pellets. Weights: ZnO-0810-A = 1.5011 g (loss 0.0012 g), B = 1.4979 g (loss 0.0008 g), C = 1.5003 g (loss 0.0008 g). Mass losses are small and consistent – likely residual binder burn-off. No visible warping or adhesion to the alumina boat.

Furnace TF-02 (1000°C) is still cooling; I will open it this afternoon.

**09:30** – Overlay of the LaB6-Si patterns (0805-A vs 0811-A). I loaded both raw data files into the analysis software. The (111) peak positions: 0805-A at 2θ = 27.28°, 0811-A at 2θ = 27.28°. The (220) peak: both at 45.44°. The (311) peak: both at 56.02°. All within 0.005°. The PI was satisfied; he noted in the margins that the two pellets are equivalent within the instrument's resolution. He initialled the overlay plot and I taped it into the back of this notebook.

CALIBRATION CERTIFICATE

Certificate No.: CAL-2026-071

Bruker D8 Advance X-ray Diffractometer

School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanyang Technological University

| SRM-1976 | Corundum (α-Al₂O₃) plate, NIST | NIST SRM 1976, Rev. B | NIST | 2027-03-15 |
| SRM-640f | Silicon powder (Si) line position standard, NIST | NIST SRM 640f | NIST | 2027-06-30 |
| LaB6-660c | Lanthanum hexaboride powder, NIST | NIST SRM 660c | NIST | 2027-01-20 |

Environmental Conditions During Calibration:
Temperature: 23.5 ± 0.8 °C
Relative Humidity: 55 ± 5 %
(As recorded by the laboratory environmental monitor, log ref. ENV-2026-071)

Procedure:
Calibration performed in accordance with SOP-MSE-XRD-014, Rev. 3, "Periodic Calibration of X-ray Diffractometer Using NIST Reference Materials."

Results:

1. Line Position Accuracy – Silicon (SRM 640f)
   Measured 2θ positions of the Si (111), (220), (311), (400), (331), and (422) reflections were compared to the certified values. The maximum deviation observed was +0.012° 2θ at the (311) reflection. All deviations were within the acceptance criterion of ±0.02° 2θ.

2. Instrumental Broadening / NIST LaB6 (SRM 660c)
   The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the LaB6 (110) reflection was measured as 0.048° 2θ. This falls within the acceptable range of 0.040° – 0.060° 2θ for the current optical configuration (0.6 mm divergence slit, 2.5° Soller slits, LynxEye XE-T detector).

3. Intensity / Alignment – Corundum (SRM 1976)
   The intensity ratio of the (104) to (113) reflections was measured as 1.02 (certified ratio: 1.00 ± 0.05). Peak height of the (104) reflection was 42,350 counts, consistent with the baseline measurements.

4. Zero-Shift Check
   The zero-shift offset, determined by scanning the direct beam and fitting the peak, was found to be -0.004° 2θ. No correction to the goniometer zero was required.

5. Detector Linearity
   Detector linearity was verified using the corundum plate over a range of tube currents (10 mA to 40 mA). The measured count rate was linear with R² = 0.9997.

Calibration Status:
The calibration certificate CAL-2026-071 states that the Bruker D8 Advance X-ray Diffractometer calibration_status is calibrated_2026-07-25. Record status: historical. The instrument is deemed to be in a calibrated state as of the date of issue and may be used for research and teaching activities in accordance with the School's Quality Manual.

documents.title: Calibration Certificate – XRD-01
documents.content:
This certificate documents the interim verification of the cooling water quality and detector
cooling circuit performance for XRD-01. The verification was performed on 4 August 2026,
following the scheduled preventive maintenance of the chiller unit (Model: Julabo F250) and
in accordance with the School's Quality Manual, Section QM-7.6 (Control of Monitoring and
Measuring Equipment).

The verification was initiated by the instrument custodian, Mr. Tan Kok Leong, after the
chiller unit was serviced. The service included replacement of the coolant, cleaning of the
heat exchanger, and replacement of the inline particulate filter. The purpose of this
verification is to confirm that the cooling water quality and flow rate are within the
manufacturer's specifications before the instrument is returned to full operational status.

---

2. COOLING WATER QUALITY

The cooling water quality was assessed using the following parameters:

2.1 Conductivity

The conductivity of the cooling water was measured using a calibrated conductivity meter
(Model: Hach sensION+ EC5, Serial No. HC-2023-118, calibrated on 12 June 2026, certificate
No. CAL-2026-048). The measurement was taken at the sampling port located at the rear of
the chiller unit, after the system had been running for 30 minutes to ensure proper
circulation and mixing.

Measured conductivity: 18.2 MΩ·cm

The water quality log MQ-04 indicates that the Milli-Q Direct Water Purification System
water_quality_conductivity_on was 18.2 MΩ·cm. This value is within the manufacturer's
specified range of 15.0 – 20.0 MΩ·cm for the cooling water circuit. The value is recorded
as current in the water quality log MQ-04, which is maintained by the Laboratory Manager
and reviewed monthly.

2.2 pH

The pH of the cooling water was measured using a calibrated pH meter (Model: Mettler Toledo
SevenCompact, Serial No. MT-2022-095, calibrated on 18 June 2026, certificate No.
CAL-2026-053).

Measured pH: 7.1 (at 25 °C)

The pH is within the specified range of 6.5 – 8.0.

2.3 Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)

The TDS was estimated from the conductivity measurement using the standard conversion
factor of 0.5 ppm per μS/cm. The conductivity of 18.2 MΩ·cm corresponds to a TDS of
approximately 0.5 ppm, which is within the specified limit of 5 ppm.

2.4 Biological Contamination

A visual inspection of the cooling water was performed, and a sample was sent for
microbiological analysis (total viable count, TVC). The analysis was performed by the
NUS Environmental Safety Office (ESO) on 4 August 2026.

Result: TVC < 1 CFU/mL (below detection limit)

The water quality log MQ-04 indicates that the Milli-Q Direct Water Purification System water_quality_conductivity_on was 18.2 MΩ·cm. Record status: current.

The TVC is within the specified limit of 100 CFU/mL.

---

3. DETECTOR COOLING CIRCUIT PERFORMANCE

3.1 Flow Rate

The coolant flow rate to the detector was measured at the inlet of the LynxEye XE-T
detector using a rotameter (Model: Key Instruments, Serial No. KI-2021-042, calibrated on
15 March 2026, certificate No. CAL-2026-019).

Measured flow rate: 1.8 L/min

The flow rate is within the manufacturer's specified range of 1.5 – 2.5 L/min.

3.2 Inlet and Outlet Temperatures

The inlet and outlet temperatures of the cooling water at the detector were measured using
a calibrated thermocouple (Model: Fluke 51 II, Serial No. FL-2020-087, calibrated on
22 April 2026, certificate No. CAL-2026-031).

Inlet temperature: 18.2 °C
Outlet temperature: 20.4 °C

The temperature differential of 2.2 °C is within the manufacturer's specified limit of
5 °C.

3.3 Pressure

The system pressure was measured at the chiller outlet and at the detector inlet.

Chiller outlet pressure: 2.1 bar
Detector inlet pressure: 1.9 bar

The pressure drop of 0.2 bar across the circuit is within the expected range, indicating
no significant blockage or restriction in the lines.

---

4. INSTRUMENT PERFORMANCE CHECKS

Following the cooling water verification, the following instrument performance checks were
performed to confirm that the instrument was operating correctly:

**3.3 Vacuum System Performance**

The vacuum system was evaluated for its ability to achieve and maintain the required pressure levels. The evacuation time from atmosphere to high vacuum (1.0 × 10⁻⁴ Pa) was measured after a 12-hour idle period.

The vacuum readings displayed on the instrument console were cross-checked against a calibrated Pirani/Penning gauge (Certificate No. VG-2026-011). The maximum deviation observed was 4%, which is within the acceptable tolerance of ±10%.

Beam current stability was assessed over a 60-minute period at an accelerating voltage of 5 kV and a probe current setting of 10 nA. Readings were recorded at 5-minute intervals.

**3.5 Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) Calibration**

The EDS detector (Oxford Instruments X-Max 80 mm²) was calibrated using a copper standard (Certificate No. CU-STD-2025-008). The Mn Kα peak at 5.895 keV was used for energy calibration, and the detector resolution was measured at the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the Mn Kα peak.

To verify overall imaging performance, a standard gold-on-carbon resolution test specimen was imaged at various magnifications. The images were assessed for sharpness, contrast, and absence of astigmatism or other aberrations.
